# @catheadowl/dsh-eval
English | 中文
**A dsh-native (dsh = DeepSeek's deepseek-harness agent CLI) agent evaluation layer for plugin autho
rs**: behavior cases run against real headless dsh traces, while review experiments test whether fre
sh models understand plugin outputs.
It evaluates the **assembled agent harness** (the graph a plugin + profile + patch + tool registry f
orm inside a real dsh headless run), not isolated functions; verdicts come from dsh-native session-t
race projections and matchers (contract assertions), not metric scores. It is not a general agent-ev
al platform (no dashboard / dataset hosting / metric catalog, no benchmark ranking) and not a DeepEv
al / OpenAI Evals replacement — those projects proved the problem space; this package picks the dsh-
native vertical solution. In deployment terms: eval frameworks embed the model calls inside the harn
ess, while task artifacts (the SWE-bench shape) ship task + fixture + verifier and let the runner su
pply the agent. This package composes the two — mock cases are credential-free artifacts judged by d
eterministic trace verifiers, real cases put the assembled harness itself (profile-supplied model in
cluded) under contract assertions, and comprehension review dispatches blank-environment reviewers —
models that see only the plugin's materialized output, nothing else — as the measuring instrument a
t the plugin's output surface, not as the subject.
> Documentation is Chinese-first; deep contracts live in docs/ (matchers / boundary contracts / revi
ew / report structure / host wiring / known issues).
## Why it exists
| Layer | Question | Granularity | Verdict | Execution |
| unit / shape test | are deterministic fields and values correct | component | automatic | the plug

in's own `node:test` |
| behavior real | does natural-language intent pick the right tool | trajecto

ry | trace matcher | dsh + real model |
| behavior mock | is the tool pipeline and write round-trip

stable | trajectory + end state | trace matcher + workspace inspect | dsh + scripted mock LLM |
| co
mprehension review | can a fresh model understand the output and the next step | rubric-primary | ma
nual rubric, converged over runs | abstract review experiment + replaceable executor |
A dsh plugin is correct when the assembled graph really wires tools, steers, prompts, and gates toge
ther — plugin unit tests cover only part of that, and "is the output understandable" is not a string
regression at all. This package turns both layers into replayable evidence instead of manual trial
ession at all. This package turns both layers into replayable evidence instead of manual trial runs.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- `src/experiment/` is the model- and runtime-agnostic experiment layer: blind review, live observat

ion, byte-identical evidence across reviewers. It does not import dsh.
- `src/adapters/dsh/` is the

landing layer: hands the abstract task to an isolated dsh headless run.
- Your `eval/` keeps only do
main fixtures, projections/observe, prompts, rubrics, and cases — no runner duplication.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Install with **npm**, host co-installed in the same tree — the verified path. Other package managers
and store layouts (e.g. a pnpm virtual store) can leave the `dsh-llm` peer without a resolvable pos
ition; for pnpm-workspace projects, give eval its own npm-managed directory (own `package.json`) ins
tead of installing into the workspace — topology notes in docs/host-wiring/README.md. Pin `@deepseek
-ai/dsh` to the same version as the CLI your profiles run on — eval drives the binary from this inst
all tree, and a driving-vs-production generation mismatch silently produces false verdicts. Run ever
ything from the package root under test (where `eval/` lives). Node `^22.19 || >=24`.
**Requirements** (wiring details and failure self-diagnostics in docs/host-wiring/README.md):
- the dsh host as a dev dependency (`@deepseek-ai/dsh`) — its dependency tree ships a same-generatio
n `dsh-llm`, so the peer needs **zero manual wiring**; a built checkout (`apps/cli/lib/bin.js`, pinn

ed via `--repo`) works as an alternative host source but is optional;
- the plugin under test instal

led into a dsh profile;
- the only form still needing manual peer wiring is an eval-only install wit
h no host in the tree (npm then auto-installs an incompatible antique `latest` of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-
llm` — see the host-wiring doc).

Install the plugin under test into the profile once — the `dsh plugin add` write face forwards to **
pnpm**, which must be on PATH (`corepack enable pnpm` or `npm i -g pnpm`) — then run; the CLIs are l
ocal bins, invoke them via `npx`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`--profile headless` is the zero-setup default — the shipped template auto-materializes in an isolat
ed home on first use. Any profile you pass must run the headless app: the case task reaches it as a
positional argument, so web-based profiles reject the run. A `dsh-eval.config.mjs` at the package ro
ot replaces the explicit flag (see "Unified config" below). A complete real-model case (`mode: 'real
'`) is in docs/intent-cases.md; real runs need a provider key by env (see docs/host-wiring/credentia
in docs/intent-cases.md; real runs need a provider key by env (see docs/host-wiring/credentials.md).

Real runs use `dsh-eval run --profile

` (the CLI resolves from the install tree; pass
`--repo <harness checkout>` to pin a built checkout instead); all flags (`--mode/--keep-artifacts/-
-fail-on-skip/--format/--report`) are documented in docs/report.md. Real cases auto-skip without cre
dentials (dsh resolves credentials itself); mock and dry runs need no credentials. The model a real
run uses comes from the chosen profile (NOT your interactive session's current pick) — provenance, h
ow to check what a run used, and how to pin it live in docs/host-wiring/model-selection.md.
